checks.ref:
command:change=$(find openspec/changes -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type d ! -name archive)
review="$change/review-specs.md"
added=$(git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- "$review" | tail -1)
base=HEAD
[ -z "$added" ] || base="$added^"
touched=$({ git diff --name-only "$base"; git ls-files -o --exclude-standard; } | sort -u | grep -vxF "$review" | grep -v '^\.gnomish-task/' || true)
[ -z "$touched" ] || { echo "$touched"; echo "the review-specs stage writes nothing but $review - restore the files above with: git checkout $base -- <file>"; exit 1; }

findings.message: R1 Fix risk is not stated honestly: Fix step (2) asserts that on touch 'the first onPointerMove reports the fraction (the browser delivers it only when it did not claim the gesture)'. With touch-action: pan-y, Chromium usually sends pointermove events within the touch slop before it sends pointercancel and starts scrolling. If so, a vertical swipe starting on a track would still pin the moment on the first small move, which is the very bug R1 reports. The Fix risk mentions only CDP stability and tap-on-release. The fix should select only once horizontal movement passes a threshold and is larger than the vertical movement (or select on pointerup when no pointercancel came), and the risk should say that browsers may send pointermove before pointercancel.

R2 cites .claude/rules/test-planning.md ('The tasks.md verification section must list concrete test commands') as its Rule, but section 8 of tasks.md already lists concrete commands, so the quote does not support the finding. Its basis is the regression risk to stable specs (openspec/specs/locations/spec.md:683 'Local time and date layout', the reorder requirements) and the Rule line should say so.
